setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Promised Land** (1 review): DeadBase comments mark this as the first Promised Land [3]
- **Hard To Handle** (1 review): Listener praises this version's strong groove [8]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Called a primal version of The Other One [11]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Energetic Not Fade Away > Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad > Not Fade Away closing segment singled out [11]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: The Promised Land [15]

## The recordings

- **gd71-05-29.aud.cotsman.19153.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 19 songs; 123 min; rated 3.27/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: Listener finds the audience recording's quality not very good; Source 1 gives most of the show in decent sound, but isn't among the era's better audience tapes [1][4]
- **gd1971-05-29.sbd.miller.110324.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 72 min; rated 4.2/5 by 10 [2]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds thick and bass-heavy, with Phil prominent; only part of the show is included; Miller's soundboard transfer sounds very close and vivid, with Phil mixed very high [9][11]

## Around the show

- DeadBase calls it the Acid Punch Show, a $2 ticket, with NRPS, R.J. Fox and James & The Good Bros [3]
- The reviewer believes this was the last acid test [3]
- Much of the crowd was reportedly dosed; the scene outside afterward was rough for unprepared people heading home [5]
- Attendee says dosed punch cups were passed around during the New Riders set, with odd characters in the lobby [7]
- Attendee recalls the scene outside the venue was definitely nuts [7]
- Taper's deck was sent back to his car at entry; he waited at the stage entrance for John McIntyre [12]
- Blog says the band coordinated one big acid test at Winterland, with hilarious results [16]
- Argues punch with acid doesn't make this an acid test; the 1971 band differed greatly from the mid-60s ones [6]
- Listener sought a Hard To Handle to top the 1971-04-28 one, and found it here [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-05-29.aud.cotsman.19153.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jim Powell, Steve Fukawa, Steve Bruzzi and Marc Pujol; source: Audience [1]. Also: Taper balanced the microphone on his head, hands-free, and reused one tape across weeks of shows; A soundboard of the second set is now available thanks to C. Miller; Two first-generation cassette sources from an unknown master were combined for this SHN set [1][12][14]
- **gd1971-05-29.sbd.miller.110324.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> CD [2]
